bayesmh

Bayesian Gaussian regression with normal and inverse-gamma priors

Stata 

bayesmh y x, likelihood(normal({var})) prior({y:}, normal(0,100)) prior({var}, igamma(1,1)) burnin(100) mcmcsize(1000) rseed(135)

R MCMCpack 

draws <- MCMCpack::MCMCregress(y ~ x, data = data, burnin = 100, mcmc = 1000, b0 = 0, B0 = .01, c0 = 2, d0 = 2, seed = 135, verbose = 0)

Differs from Stata Gaussian regression only. The coefficient priors are independent N(0, 100); B0 = .01 is their precision. c0 = d0 = 2 gives an inverse-gamma(1, 1) prior on residual variance. The returned draws object is a coda mcmc chain. Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings samplers differ; these short chains illustrate syntax, not convergence.

Stata reference · R reference

bayespredict

Posterior mean Gaussian regression response

Stata 

bayespredict pmean, mean

R brms 

data$pmean <- stats::predict(fit, newdata = data, summary = TRUE, robust = FALSE)[, "Estimate"]

Differs from Stata fit must be an existing univariate brmsfit using the same likelihood, predictors and priors as the Stata model; data contains prediction rows. predict.brmsfit summarizes simulated outcomes including observation noise. Its mean estimates the posterior predictive mean. Match group-level-effect treatment where applicable; Monte Carlo samples differ.

Stata reference · R reference

bayesreps

Replicated outcomes from a Gaussian posterior predictive distribution

Stata 

bayesreps yrep*, nreps(10)

R brms 

t(brms::posterior_predict(fit, newdata = data, ndraws = 10))

Differs from Stata fit must be an existing univariate brmsfit matching the Stata model likelihood, predictors and priors. Returns observations by 10 posterior predictive replicates, including observation noise. brms randomly selects posterior draws; match group-level-effect treatment where applicable. Random draws and storage differ from Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

bayesstats

Effective MCMC sample size

Stata 

bayesstats ess

R coda 

{ ess <- coda::effectiveSize(draws); data.frame(ess = ess, correlation_time = nrow(draws) / ess, efficiency = ess / nrow(draws)) }

Differs from Stata draws must be one coda mcmc chain after warmup. Reports ESS, correlation time (draw count / ESS) and efficiency (ESS / draw count). coda uses an autoregressive spectral estimate, whereas Stata truncates sample autocorrelations; numerical diagnostics differ.

Stata reference · R reference

Posterior means, standard deviations and quantiles

Stata 

bayesstats summary

R posterior 

posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(draws), mean, sd, mcse = posterior::mcse_mean, median, ~stats::quantile(.x, probs = c(.025, .975)))

Differs from Stata draws must be a coda mcmc or mcmc.list object containing posterior parameter draws, for example the result of MCMCpack::MCMCregress(). Reports means, SDs, MCSEs, medians and 95% equal-tailed intervals. MCSE algorithms differ from Stata. Transform draws before summarizing a transformed parameter.

Stata reference · R reference

Posterior summary of a transformed coefficient

Stata 

bayesstats summary (effect:exp({y:x}))

R posterior 

posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(coda::mcmc(exp(as.matrix(draws)[, "x", drop = FALSE]))), mean, sd, mcse = posterior::mcse_mean, median, ~stats::quantile(.x, probs = c(.025, .975)))

Differs from Stata draws must be a coda mcmc or mcmc.list object containing posterior parameter draws, for example the result of MCMCpack::MCMCregress(). Reports means, SDs, MCSEs, medians and 95% equal-tailed intervals. MCSE algorithms differ from Stata. Transform draws before summarizing a transformed parameter.

Stata reference · R reference

Ninety-percent highest-posterior-density interval

Stata 

bayesstats summary {y:x}, hpd clevel(90)

R posterior 

posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(draws[, "x", drop = FALSE]), mean, sd, mcse = posterior::mcse_mean, median, hpd = ~coda::HPDinterval(coda::mcmc(.x), prob = .9)[1, ])

Differs from Stata draws is a single coda mcmc chain with column x. Reports posterior summaries and a 90% shortest contiguous HPD interval, rather than interval endpoints alone. Multimodal posteriors may not have a single HPD interval; MCSE algorithms differ from Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

bayestest

Posterior probability of a positive slope

Stata 

bayestest interval {y:x}, lower(0)

R posterior 

posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(coda::mcmc(1 * (draws[, "x", drop = FALSE] > 0))), mean, sd, mcse = posterior::mcse_mean)

Differs from Stata draws is one coda mcmc chain with parameter x. Summarizes the interval-membership indicator: its mean is the posterior probability, with SD and MCSE. Bounds are strict. MCSE algorithms differ from Stata; a constant indicator may give undefined MCSE. This is not a Bayes factor or a frequentist p-value.

Stata reference · R reference

Posterior probability within a substantive effect interval

Stata 

bayestest interval {y:x}, lower(1.8) upper(2.2)

R posterior 

posterior::summarise_draws(posterior::as_draws_array(coda::mcmc(1 * (draws[, "x", drop = FALSE] > 1.8 & draws[, "x", drop = FALSE] < 2.2))), mean, sd, mcse = posterior::mcse_mean)

Differs from Stata draws is one coda mcmc chain with parameter x. Summarizes the interval-membership indicator: its mean is the posterior probability, with SD and MCSE. Bounds are strict. MCSE algorithms differ from Stata; a constant indicator may give undefined MCSE. This is not a Bayes factor or a frequentist p-value.
